comment: Sites exercising docs/GENERATION.md §4, one per canonical situation. Mined from data/overture-ch/preview.arpa (Montreux extract, z16) with `arpentry_verify <archive> --mine`. Each is the strongest instance the data holds, not a guess: re-mine after retiling a different extract. Use with `arpentry_verify <archive> --scenario S5`.

sites.source: mined: motorway deck standing 75 m above the drawn ground — the tallest viaduct in the extract, and worth confirming is real rather than phantom
mined: footway deck clearing the ground by only 2 m — S1's degenerate case, a deck that is nearly a chord
mined: 9 decks over at-grade road in one tile, all at level 1 — the densest crossing stack in the extract
mined: narrow_gauge bore under 599 m of hill — the deepest cover in the extract; a plausible Alpine rail tunnel, but the depth is worth confirming against the level ordinal it came from
mined: 6 bores under an at-grade road — the urban underpass case
mined: a deck and a bore in the same tile — bridge into tunnel, or close enough to inspect
mined: at-grade road at 28 % grade — the steepest carriageway still plausible as a real road, where the correct action is to do nothing

unsited.why: River bridge on flat ground. Needs the water layer decoded to find a deck over a river rather than over a ravine; the verifier reads only terrain and transportation today.

Dual carriageway on one structure. Needs parallel-structure identity, which the archive does not carry — two decks side by side are indistinguishable from one dual deck. Site by hand from the solved model (graph::parallel_structure_unions).
Annotation noise. Defined by its input, not its output: the site is a span that overlaps or leaves a sliver in the source, so it must come from the scene graph, not the archive.
Building on a steep slope. Needs the building layer decoded.
Dense old town with courtyards. Needs the building layer decoded.
Building beside a road cut. Needs the building layer decoded.
Lakefront. Needs the water layer decoded. Lake Geneva is in the extract, so this is the cheapest of the seven to add.
